entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Emperor Xiaomin of Northern Zhou (周孝閔帝), personal name Yuwen Jue (宇文覺), nickname Dharani (陀羅尼), was the founder of the Xianbei-led Northern Zhou dynasty of China, ruling as Heavenly Prince. He was the heir of Western Wei's paramount general Yuwen Tai, and after Yuwen Tai's death in 556, his cousin Yuwen Hu, serving as his guardian, forced Emperor Gong of Western Wei to yield the throne to Yuwen Jue in spring 557, establishing Northern Zhou. Later in 557, however, Yuwen Jue, wanting to assume power more quickly, led a campaign that resulted in the capture of the capital city of Luoyang, which had been held by the Chen dynasty, and the subsequent surrender of the remaining Chen forces. This campaign marked a significant turning point in Northern Zhou's history, as it allowed the dynasty to assert its dominance over the region and establish a stable government. In 558, Yuwen Jue issued the 'Edict of the Northern Zhou', which standardized the Chinese calendar, currency, and weights and measures, and promoted the use of the Chinese language as the official language of the dynasty. The Edict also established the Northern Zhou as a major center of culture and learning, attracting scholars and intellectuals from across the region. Yuwen Jue's legacy as a wise and just ruler continued to shape Northern Zhou's history, as he implemented policies aimed at promoting economic growth and social stability. He died in 557 CE, but his impact on the region was felt for centuries to come.
